items.name: Contract Execution
items.summary: Governs how binding agreements are signed and preserved across ABC Insurance Group, ensuring that only authorized officers commit the company and that every executed contract is recoverable from a single system of record.

subs.title: Signature Authority Matrix
subs.description: A board-approved matrix defines which officers and delegates may execute agreements, tiered by contract value, duration, and risk class (e.g., reinsurance treaties, producer agreements, vendor contracts). Signatures outside the matrix are invalid and must be escalated to the General Counsel for ratification or rescission. The matrix is reviewed annually and updated within 30 days of any officer change.

subs.title: Fully Executed Copies Retained
subs.description: A complete, countersigned copy of every agreement, including all exhibits, schedules, and amendments, must be captured in the contract repository within 5 business days of execution. Paper originals for instruments requiring wet signatures, such as certain reinsurance and regulatory filings, are retained by Legal Operations with the repository record noting their physical location.

subs.title: Contract Lifecycle Management System Required
subs.description: All contracts must be created, routed, executed, and stored through the enterprise CLM platform; side agreements held in email or shared drives are prohibited. The CLM record is the authoritative source for contract status, parties, value, and key dates used by Finance, Procurement, and Compliance reporting.

items.name: Contract Lifecycle
items.summary: Establishes post-signature stewardship of the contract portfolio so that commitments are honored, renewals are deliberate decisions rather than accidents, and expiring agreements never leave the carrier without coverage, services, or distribution capacity.

subs.title: Renewal Tracking
subs.description: Every contract with a renewal or auto-renewal provision carries CLM-managed alerts beginning at least 90 days before the renewal or non-renewal notice deadline, with longer lead times for reinsurance treaties and core system vendors. The business owner must record an affirmative renew, renegotiate, or terminate decision before the notice window closes.

subs.title: Obligation Monitoring
subs.description: Material obligations such as service levels, insurance and security requirements, audit rights, and regulatory flow-down clauses are extracted into the CLM at onboarding and assigned to a named business owner. Owners attest to compliance status at least quarterly, and breaches by either party are escalated to Legal for cure-notice or remediation handling.

subs.title: Termination and Expiration Management
subs.description: Terminations follow a documented close-out checklist covering final payments, return or destruction of policyholder and company data, transition assistance, and survival-clause obligations. Expired and terminated contracts are marked closed in the CLM and retained per the records schedule rather than deleted.

items.name: Contract Review Process
items.summary: Defines when and how the Legal department reviews inbound and outbound agreements, ensuring material commitments receive qualified legal scrutiny while keeping negotiations consistent and auditable.

subs.title: Legal Review of All Contracts Over $50K
subs.description: Any agreement with total expected value above $50,000, and any contract involving policyholder data, reinsurance, or regulatory undertakings regardless of value, must be reviewed and cleared by a Legal attorney before signature. Business units may not split contracts to fall under the threshold, and the reviewing attorney is recorded in the CLM.

subs.title: Standard Playbook
subs.description: Negotiations are conducted against a Legal-maintained playbook that specifies preferred, fallback, and walk-away positions for recurring clauses such as limitation of liability, indemnification, data protection, and insurance requirements. Positions outside the playbook require attorney sign-off, and the playbook is refreshed at least annually to reflect new regulatory and market conditions.

subs.title: Redline Tracking
subs.description: All negotiated changes must be exchanged as tracked revisions and stored as versioned documents in the CLM so the negotiation history is reconstructible. Final execution versions are compared against the last agreed redline to confirm no unapproved language was introduced.

items.name: Contract Templates
items.summary: Maintains a library of pre-approved agreement forms so routine contracting moves quickly on terms Legal has already vetted, concentrating attorney effort on genuinely novel or high-risk deals.

subs.title: Approved Templates for Common Agreements
subs.description: Legal publishes and owns standard templates for recurring agreement types, including NDAs, producer and agency agreements, vendor services agreements, statements of work, and data processing addenda. Templates embed ABC Insurance Group's required clauses on confidentiality, regulatory compliance, and audit rights, and only the current CLM-published version may be used.

subs.title: Deviation Requires Legal Approval
subs.description: Any edit to template language beyond designated fill-in fields must be approved by a Legal attorney before the document is sent to a counterparty. Approved deviations are logged with rationale so frequently requested changes can be evaluated for incorporation into the next template revision.

items.name: Employment Agreements
items.summary: Governs the legal documentation of the employment relationship from offer through start date, protecting the carrier's confidential underwriting, pricing, and customer information while ensuring hires are made on consistent, defensible terms.

subs.title: Standardized Offer Letters
subs.description: All offers of employment use Legal-approved letter templates with role-appropriate variants for licensed producers, executives, and standard staff. Compensation terms, contingencies such as background checks and licensing verification, and at-will language may not be modified without Legal and HR approval.

subs.title: Non-Compete and NDA Requirements
subs.description: Confidentiality agreements are required for all employees before access to company systems, and restrictive covenants such as non-competition and non-solicitation provisions are applied only to roles where they are justified and enforceable under the governing state's law. Legal maintains state-specific covenant language and reviews enforceability annually as statutes change.

subs.title: Onboarding Compliance
subs.description: New-hire onboarding must capture executed employment documents, I-9 verification, and any required insurance licensing or appointment paperwork before the employee begins regulated work. HR confirms completion in the HRIS, and missing items trigger escalation within the first week of employment.

items.name: Termination Review
items.summary: Ensures employee separations are executed consistently and lawfully, managing litigation exposure and protecting company assets and policyholder data when staff depart.

subs.title: Termination Checklist
subs.description: Every separation follows a standard checklist covering final pay and benefits compliance, system and facility access revocation, recovery of company property, and termination of any state insurance appointments held by the departing employee. The completed checklist is retained in the personnel file.

subs.title: Legal Review for Risk
subs.description: Before an involuntary termination is communicated, Legal assesses risk factors including protected-class considerations, recent complaints or whistleblower activity, pending leave or accommodation requests, and documentation adequacy. High-risk separations require written Legal clearance and may be restructured or delayed pending remediation.

subs.title: Separation Agreement Templates
subs.description: Where severance is offered, Legal-maintained separation agreement templates are used, incorporating jurisdiction-specific release requirements such as ADEA consideration and revocation periods. Template deviations and individually negotiated terms require attorney approval before presentation to the employee.

items.name: Board Materials
items.summary: Sets the preparation and distribution discipline for board and committee materials so directors of ABC Insurance Group receive accurate, consistent, and legally vetted information with enough time to discharge their oversight duties.

subs.title: Materials Distributed Five Days in Advance
subs.description: Complete board and committee packets must be posted to the secure board portal no later than five business days before the meeting. Late additions require Corporate Secretary approval and are flagged as supplemental, and chronic late submissions are reported to the committee chair.

subs.title: Standardized Format
subs.description: All submissions follow the Corporate Secretary's templates, including an executive summary, requested action or resolution language, risk and regulatory implications, and supporting detail. Consistent structure lets directors compare items across meetings and supports an orderly minute-taking and resolution record.

subs.title: General Counsel Review Required
subs.description: The General Counsel or a designee reviews every packet before distribution for legal accuracy, privilege protection, disclosure consistency, and alignment with prior board actions. Items presenting material legal or regulatory exposure carry an explicit Legal assessment in the materials.

items.name: Board Minutes
items.summary: Governs the creation, approval, and preservation of the official record of board and committee proceedings, which regulators and examiners rely on as primary evidence of director oversight at an insurance holding company.

subs.title: Draft Minutes Within Seven Days
subs.description: The Corporate Secretary circulates draft minutes to the chair within seven calendar days of each meeting while discussion and dissents are fresh. Drafts record attendance, quorum, matters considered, resolutions adopted, and abstentions or recusals, at a level of detail consistent with privilege and litigation considerations.

subs.title: Approved at Next Meeting
subs.description: Minutes are presented for formal approval as the first order of business at the following meeting of the same body, with corrections captured in the approving meeting's record. Unapproved minutes are clearly marked as drafts and are not released to examiners or auditors without Corporate Secretary direction.

subs.title: Signed and Retained
subs.description: Approved minutes are signed by the Corporate Secretary, entered into the official minute books, and retained permanently in accordance with corporate records requirements and state insurance examination expectations. Access to minute books is restricted and logged.

items.name: Entity Management
items.summary: Maintains the legal health of every company in the ABC Insurance Group holding system, ensuring each insurance subsidiary and affiliate remains in good standing with state regulators and secretaries of state.

subs.title: Current Entity Inventory
subs.description: Legal maintains a complete register of all legal entities, including each insurer's domicile, licenses, NAIC company code, officers and directors, and ownership within the holding company structure. The inventory is reconciled quarterly against state records and the Schedule Y organizational chart, and changes such as formations, mergers, or dissolutions are recorded within 10 business days.

subs.title: Registered Agent Maintained
subs.description: Every entity must have a current registered agent in each jurisdiction where it is formed or qualified to do business, so that service of process, regulatory notices, and policyholder suits are received and routed reliably. Agent appointments are verified annually and updated immediately upon any agent or address change.

subs.title: Annual Filings on Time
subs.description: Annual reports, franchise tax filings, and corporate registrations are tracked on a compliance calendar with owners and lead-time alerts, and no entity may lapse into delinquent status. Filing confirmations are stored with the entity record, and any notice of pending forfeiture is escalated to the General Counsel the day it is received.

items.name: Invention Disclosure
items.summary: Channels employee innovations, such as underwriting models, claims automation, and insurtech tooling, into a formal evaluation pipeline so the company captures, protects, and clearly owns the intellectual property it creates.

subs.title: Invention Disclosure Process
subs.description: Employees and contractors submit potentially protectable innovations through a standard disclosure form capturing the problem solved, technical approach, contributors, and any public exposure or third-party components. Legal acknowledges receipt, logs the disclosure in the IP register, and triages it for evaluation within 30 days.

subs.title: Patentability Assessment
subs.description: Disclosed inventions are assessed by IP counsel for novelty, subject-matter eligibility, and commercial value to the insurance business, with a documented decision to pursue patent protection, hold as a trade secret, or release. Time-sensitive items, such as inventions nearing public demonstration, are expedited to preserve filing rights.

subs.title: Assignment Agreements
subs.description: All employees sign invention assignment provisions at hire, and contractors and development vendors must execute work-for-hire or present assignment terms before development begins. Legal verifies the chain of title for each disclosure and cures any gaps with confirmatory assignments before filing or asserting rights.

items.name: Trademark Management
items.summary: Protects the ABC Insurance Group brand and product names that policyholders and producers rely on, keeping registrations enforceable and acting against confusingly similar uses in the insurance marketplace.

subs.title: Trademark Portfolio
subs.description: Legal maintains a register of all house marks, product names, and logos, recording registration status, classes, and jurisdictions for each. New product or program names proposed by the business must be cleared through a trademark search and Legal approval before market use or filing.

subs.title: Renewal Tracking
subs.description: Registration maintenance deadlines, including declarations of use and renewal windows, are docketed with alerts at least six months in advance so no mark lapses unintentionally. Renewal decisions weigh continued commercial use, and abandonments are deliberate, documented choices approved by IP counsel.

subs.title: Infringement Monitoring
subs.description: Watch services and periodic marketplace reviews surface confusingly similar marks, domain names, and look-alike insurance offerings, which matter because imposter brands create direct consumer-harm and regulatory exposure for a carrier. Detected conflicts are assessed within 30 days and addressed through escalating responses from demand letters to opposition or litigation.

items.name: Legal Spend Management
items.summary: Brings financial discipline to the legal function, giving Finance and the General Counsel an accurate, current view of legal costs and driving the total cost of legal services down without degrading outcomes.

subs.title: Budget Tracking
subs.description: Legal operates an annual budget broken down by practice area and matter type, with actuals tracked monthly through the e-billing system. Variances above 10% at the practice-area level require a documented explanation and a reforecast submitted to Finance.

subs.title: Accruals
subs.description: Outside counsel and vendor work performed but not yet invoiced is accrued monthly so legal expense lands in the correct accounting period, supporting accurate statutory and GAAP reporting. Firms must submit accrual estimates by the monthly deadline, and persistent non-compliance affects panel standing.

subs.title: Outside Counsel Spend Analysis
subs.description: Spend is analyzed at least quarterly by firm, matter type, timekeeper level, and rate, benchmarking effective rates and matter costs against prior periods and market data. The analysis feeds rate negotiations, panel reviews, and decisions about which work to move to lower-cost firms or in-house staff.

subs.title: Cost Reduction
subs.description: Legal Operations maintains an active cost-reduction agenda including alternative fee arrangements, insourcing of repeatable work, use of staffing levels appropriate to matter complexity, and competitive bidding for significant matters. Savings initiatives carry quantified targets and are reported to the General Counsel semiannually.

items.name: Legal Technology
items.summary: Defines the technology backbone of the legal department so legal work is conducted in supported systems with trustworthy data, rather than scattered across inboxes and spreadsheets.

subs.title: CLM, E-Billing, and Matter Management Systems
subs.description: The department's core platforms, contract lifecycle management, electronic billing, and matter management, are the mandatory systems of record for contracts, invoices, and legal matters respectively. New legal tools must be procured through IT and Legal Operations governance, integrate with these core systems where applicable, and meet the carrier's information security standards for handling confidential and policyholder data.

subs.title: Data Standards
subs.description: Common reference data, including matter types, practice areas, entity names, and cost centers, follows controlled picklists aligned to Finance and enterprise data definitions. Required fields are enforced at intake so records are complete at creation, and data quality is sampled quarterly with correction assignments for owning teams.

subs.title: Reporting
subs.description: Standard dashboards covering matter volumes, cycle times, contract turnaround, and spend are produced from the core systems on a defined monthly and quarterly cadence for the General Counsel and business partners. Ad hoc reporting requests are fulfilled from system data, not manually maintained shadow trackers.

items.name: Litigation Hold
items.summary: Ensures potentially relevant evidence is preserved the moment litigation or a regulatory proceeding becomes reasonably anticipated, protecting the carrier from spoliation sanctions in claims disputes, bad-faith actions, and market conduct matters.

subs.title: Hold Notice Within 24 Hours of Trigger
subs.description: When Legal identifies a preservation trigger, such as a suit, demand letter, regulatory subpoena, or a claim flagged for bad-faith exposure, a written hold notice is issued to identified custodians and to IT within 24 hours. The notice describes the matter, the categories of records to preserve, including emails, claim files, underwriting files, and recorded calls, and suspends routine deletion for affected data sources.

subs.title: Custodian Acknowledgment Tracked
subs.description: Each custodian must affirmatively acknowledge the hold, and acknowledgments are tracked in the matter management system with escalation to the custodian's manager after 5 business days of non-response. Holds are re-confirmed periodically for long-running matters, custodian lists are updated as employees join or leave, and releases are issued in writing only when Legal closes the preservation obligation.

items.name: Matter Management
items.summary: Provides a single, current operating picture of the company's disputes and significant legal matters so exposure can be reserved, reported, and managed rather than discovered late.

subs.title: All Matters Logged in System
subs.description: Every litigation, arbitration, regulatory enforcement, and significant pre-suit dispute is opened in the matter management system within 5 business days of Legal becoming aware of it, with assigned counsel, opposing parties, jurisdiction, and an initial exposure assessment. Off-system matters are prohibited, and matters meeting materiality thresholds are flagged for Finance reserve evaluation and disclosure review.

subs.title: Budget Tracking
subs.description: Significant matters carry a phase-based budget agreed with outside counsel at the outset and revised at major case milestones. Actual fees and costs are tracked against budget in the e-billing system, and projected overruns above 15% require written justification and in-house counsel approval before further spend.

subs.title: Monthly Status Updates
subs.description: Responsible attorneys record a substantive status entry for each active matter at least monthly, covering recent developments, upcoming deadlines, and any change in exposure or strategy. These updates feed the litigation report provided to the General Counsel and support quarterly loss-contingency reviews with Finance and external auditors.

items.name: Outside Counsel
items.summary: Controls how external law firms are selected, engaged, and paid, ensuring the carrier gets consistent quality and pricing from firms that understand insurance defense, coverage, and regulatory work.

subs.title: Approved Panel
subs.description: Outside work is placed with firms on the Legal-maintained approved panel, selected for insurance-sector expertise, jurisdictional coverage, rates, and conflict posture. Off-panel engagements require General Counsel approval with documented rationale, and the panel is formally reviewed at least every two years against performance and spend data.

subs.title: Engagement Letters
subs.description: Each new firm relationship, and each significant new matter, is governed by an executed engagement letter specifying scope, staffing, rates, conflict and confidentiality terms, and data-handling obligations appropriate to policyholder information. No work may begin or be paid without the engagement letter on file.

subs.title: Billing Guidelines
subs.description: All panel firms are bound by ABC Insurance Group's outside counsel billing guidelines, which set task-based billing requirements, staffing expectations, non-billable activities, and expense rules. Guidelines are incorporated into every engagement, and repeated violations are grounds for fee adjustment or panel removal.

subs.title: Invoice Review
subs.description: Firm invoices are submitted through the e-billing system, where automated rules and reviewing attorneys check them against guidelines, budgets, and the work actually performed. Non-compliant line items are adjusted or rejected with reasons returned to the firm, and approved invoices route to payment within agreed terms.

items.name: Data Processing Agreements
items.summary: Ensures every third party that touches personal data, including policyholder, claimant, and employee information, is bound by contractual privacy and security obligations that satisfy state insurance data security laws and consumer privacy statutes.

subs.title: DPA Required for Vendors Handling Personal Data
subs.description: No vendor, TPA, MGA, or other service provider may receive or process personal data until a data processing agreement or equivalent addendum is executed. The requirement applies regardless of contract value and covers data such as claims files, medical records, and producer-collected applicant information, consistent with obligations under GLBA, HIPAA where applicable, and state insurance data security laws modeled on the NAIC standard.

subs.title: Standard Clauses
subs.description: Legal maintains standard DPA language covering processing limitations, confidentiality, security controls, breach notification within defined timeframes, subprocessor restrictions, audit rights, and return or destruction of data at termination. The standard terms are updated as state privacy laws and regulatory expectations evolve, and counterparty-proposed alternatives are measured against them.

subs.title: Review Process
subs.description: Negotiated DPAs are reviewed by privacy counsel in coordination with Information Security, which validates that promised technical and organizational measures match the vendor's actual assessment results. Approved DPAs are linked to the master agreement in the CLM and re-examined when the scope of data sharing materially changes.

items.name: Data Subject Requests
items.summary: Governs the intake and fulfillment of consumer privacy rights requests, such as access, deletion, and correction, so policyholders and other individuals receive lawful, timely responses and the carrier can demonstrate compliance to regulators.

subs.title: Documented DSR Process
subs.description: A written procedure defines how requests are received across channels including web forms, call centers, and agents, how requester identity is verified, and how data is located across policy administration, claims, and marketing systems. The procedure also addresses insurance-specific exceptions, such as records that must be retained for claims handling, fraud investigation, or statutory record-keeping despite a deletion request.

subs.title: Response Within Regulatory Timeline
subs.description: Each request is responded to within the deadline of the applicable statute, typically 45 days under state consumer privacy laws, with extensions invoked and communicated only as the law permits. Internal milestones are set ahead of the legal deadline, and at-risk requests are escalated to the privacy officer before the date is missed.

subs.title: Logging Required
subs.description: Every request is logged with receipt date, requester category, verification outcome, actions taken, and response date, creating an auditable record of rights fulfillment. The log is reviewed quarterly for timeliness and volume trends and serves as primary evidence in regulatory examinations and inquiries.

items.name: Privacy Impact Assessments
items.summary: Requires privacy risk to be evaluated before new uses of personal data go live, so initiatives like AI-assisted underwriting, telematics programs, and new marketing analytics are designed lawfully rather than remediated after launch.

subs.title: PIA Required for New Processing
subs.description: A privacy impact assessment must be completed before launching any new or materially changed processing of personal data, including new systems, vendor integrations, data sharing arrangements, and models that score or profile consumers. Projects subject to heightened regulatory scrutiny, such as algorithmic underwriting or use of sensitive health data, automatically require a full assessment.

subs.title: Standardized Template
subs.description: Assessments use the privacy office's standard template, which captures data elements and sources, purposes, legal basis, retention, third-party transfers, and identified risks with mitigations. The uniform format makes assessments comparable across business lines and ready for production to regulators on request.

subs.title: Approval Workflow
subs.description: Completed assessments route through a defined workflow for privacy counsel review, with Information Security and Compliance sign-off where their domains are implicated. Processing may not begin until approval is recorded, and conditions attached to approval are tracked to closure by the project owner.

items.name: Regulatory Filings
items.summary: Brings discipline to the heavy filing obligations of a multi-state insurer, from holding company and rate or form filings to corporate registrations, so nothing required by a regulator is late, unowned, or unreviewed.

subs.title: Filing Calendar
subs.description: All recurring regulatory filings, including holding company filings such as Form B and enterprise risk reports, state corporate registrations, and Legal-owned components of financial and market conduct submissions, are maintained on a centralized compliance calendar. Each entry carries due dates, lead times, and automated reminders, and the calendar is reconciled annually against current statutory requirements in every licensed state.

subs.title: Ownership Assigned
subs.description: Every filing has a named preparer and a named accountable owner responsible for on-time, accurate submission, with documented backups to cover absences and turnover. Ownership changes are updated on the calendar immediately, and unowned filings are treated as a control deficiency reported to the General Counsel.

subs.title: Review Process
subs.description: Filings undergo a second-person review proportionate to their significance before submission, with material filings, such as those affecting the holding company structure or regulatory commitments, reviewed by senior counsel. Reviewers verify accuracy, consistency with prior filings, and proper signatory authority.

subs.title: Retention Requirements
subs.description: As-filed copies, regulator acknowledgments, and supporting workpapers are retained under the records retention schedule and remain readily retrievable for state examinations. Retention periods meet or exceed the longest applicable statutory requirement across the jurisdictions where the filing was made.

items.name: Regulatory Inquiries
items.summary: Standardizes how the company responds when insurance departments and other regulators ask questions, from routine consumer complaint referrals to market conduct exams and subpoenas, ensuring responses are accurate, privileged where appropriate, and never late.

subs.title: Response Protocol
subs.description: All regulatory inquiries, including DOI consumer complaint referrals, data calls, exam requests, and subpoenas, are routed to Legal upon receipt and logged in the matter management system. The protocol designates a single coordinating attorney per inquiry, defines who may communicate with the regulator, and prohibits business units from responding directly without Legal clearance.

subs.title: Privilege Review
subs.description: Documents and draft responses are reviewed for attorney-client privilege and work product before production, with privileged materials withheld or logged as the situation requires. Counsel also evaluates confidentiality protections available for produced materials, such as state exam confidentiality statutes and trade secret designations.

subs.title: Coordination with Business
subs.description: The coordinating attorney works with the affected business units, such as Claims, Underwriting, or Distribution, to gather accurate facts and records, and validates business-drafted content before it goes to the regulator. Business stakeholders are briefed on inquiry status and on any remediation commitments made in the response.

subs.title: Timeline Tracking
subs.description: Regulator deadlines and any granted extensions are docketed with internal due dates set in advance of the official date. Aging open inquiries are reviewed at least monthly, and any response at risk of missing a regulatory deadline is escalated to the General Counsel before the deadline passes.

items.name: Legal Training
items.summary: Equips employees outside the legal department to recognize and handle the legal dimensions of their work, reducing the contract, privacy, and regulatory missteps that originate in the business before Legal ever sees them.

subs.title: Contract Basics for Business
subs.description: Employees who request, negotiate, or manage contracts complete training on the contracting lifecycle, including when Legal review is required, how to use approved templates and the CLM, signature authority limits, and the risks of side agreements or verbal commitments. Completion is required before an employee is granted contract-initiation access in the CLM.

subs.title: Compliance Awareness
subs.description: General awareness training covers the legal topics most likely to arise in an insurance carrier's daily operations, including privacy and safeguarding of policyholder information, litigation holds and records preservation, unfair trade practice basics, and when to escalate to Legal. Content is tailored by role, with deeper modules for claims, underwriting, and distribution staff.

subs.title: Annual Updates
subs.description: Training content is refreshed at least annually to reflect new statutes, regulatory developments, and lessons learned from internal incidents and examinations, and employees complete recertification on the updated material each year. Completion rates are tracked by HR and reported to the General Counsel, with follow-up for delinquent employees and their managers.
